q: Radionuclides found in ________ are potassium-40, radium-226, and radium-228. (2024)
e: Potassium-40, radium-226, and radium-228 are naturally occurring radionuclides found in water.

q: Vegetables and other waste materials can also be used to produce _______ fuels. (2025)
e: Waste materials and vegetables are used to produce greener fuels like biofuels.

q: The burning of large quantities of fossil fuels, especially coal, releases larger amounts of ________ gas into the atmosphere. (2024)
e: Burning coal and fossil fuels releases significant amounts of hydrogen sulphide gas into the atmosphere.

q: Which of the following is an extremely potent pollutant? (2025)
e: Nuclear waste is an extremely potent pollutant due to its high level of radiation.

q: Methanol is produced from ________ and hydrogen. (2026)
e: Methanol is commercially produced by reacting carbon monoxide with hydrogen.

q: Cadmium exists as the ________ oxidation state in nature. (2024)
e: Cadmium typically exists in the +2 oxidation state in natural compounds.

q: The cycling of elements is interconnected with the ________ cycle. (2025)
e: The water cycle acts as a major transport medium that interconnects biogeochemical cycles.

q: ________ and X-rays can cause severe damage to the cell. (2025)
e: Gamma rays and X-rays have high penetrating power and cause severe cellular damage.

q: In the nitrogen cycle, the conversion of nitrates to nitrogen is called ________. (2024)
e: Denitrification is the biological process that converts nitrates into nitrogen gas.

q: Beta particles can penetrate ________. (2026)
e: Beta particles easily penetrate thin, low-density materials like paper.

q: ________ has the highest penetrating power. (2025)
e: Gamma rays possess the highest penetrating power among radiation types.

q: What is the impact of ocean acidification on marine life? (2025)
a: Harm to shell fish and coral
e: Ocean acidification harms calcifying organisms such as shellfish and coral reefs.

q: ________ enters the atmosphere largely in the exhaust fumes from internal combustion engine. (2024)
e: Lead enters the atmosphere primarily through internal combustion engine emissions.

q: ________ are chemically stable, remain intact in the environment for long period. (2025)
e: Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs) resist environmental degradation and remain intact long-term.

q: Choose the fissile nuclides from the following. (2026)
e: Plutonium-239 (Pu-239) is a fissile nuclide capable of sustaining nuclear fission.

q: The oceans also obtain carbon from the ________ by absorbing carbon dioxide. (2025)
e: Oceans absorb carbon dioxide directly from the Earth's atmosphere.

q: ________ are derived from renewable biomass sources such as corn starch, vegetable oils and fats. (2026)
e: Bioplastics are plastics manufactured from renewable biomass sources such as corn starch and vegetable oils.

q: ________ is considered a renewable energy source. (2024)
e: Solar energy is an infinitely renewable energy source.

q: The guano of marine birds contains a high level of ________. (2024)
e: Guano from marine birds contains high amounts of phosphorous.

q: Glucose can be converted into ________ acid by an enzyme discovered in genetically modified bacteria. (2025)
e: Genetically modified bacteria can biosynthesize adipic acid from glucose.

q: The fissile nuclide is ________. (2026)
e: Pu-239 is classified as a fissile nuclide.

q: ________ cannot be found in a gaseous state in the biogeochemical cycle. (2024)
e: Phosphorus does not enter a gaseous state in its natural biogeochemical cycle.

q: Radioactivity is the characteristic of which of the following? (2025)
e: Radioactivity is an intrinsic property of an unstable atomic nucleus.

q: Which of the following pollutants is responsible for the phenomenon known as acid rain? (2026)
e: Sulfur dioxide (SO2) reacts with atmospheric moisture to form acid rain.

q: ________ is a standard substrate for the production of adipic acid. (2025)
e: Benzene is the primary substrate used in the industrial synthesis of adipic acid.

q: The ________ is used as a source of alpha particles in ionisation smoke detectors. (2026)
e: Americium-241 (Am-241) emits alpha particles used in ionization smoke detectors.

q: Traces of radioactive materials can be found in the body, mainly naturally occurring ________. (2025)
e: Potassium-40 is a major naturally occurring radioactive isotope in living bodies.

q: The process did not involve in the carbon cycles are ________. (2024)
e: Ammonification is part of the nitrogen cycle rather than the carbon cycle.

q: Tobacco smoking is also a significant source of ________ exposure. (2025)
e: Tobacco smoke contains high levels of cadmium.

q: ________ cycle does not involve the atmosphere. (2026)
e: The phosphorus cycle is a sedimentary cycle that does not involve the atmosphere.

q: The guano of marine birds contains a high level of ________. (2025)
e: Marine bird guano contains a high level of phosphorus.

q: Arsenic is mostly found in the form of + 3 and ________ oxidation states. (2025)
e: Arsenic predominantly exists in the +3 and +5 oxidation states.

q: ________ is used to kill some parasites in fruit cultivation and potato growing. (2025)
e: Sodium arsenate is used to eradicate specific parasites in crops like fruit and potatoes.

q: Benzene is a standard substrate for the production of ________ acid. (2026)
e: Benzene is a starting substrate for manufacturing adipic acid.

q: Traces of radioactive materials can be found in the body, mainly naturally occurring ________. (2026)
e: Potassium-40 is naturally found inside the biological organism.

q: ________ is one of the components that make up proteins and vitamins. (2026)
e: Sulphur is a key component found in proteins and certain vitamins.

q: A radionuclide is an atom with an unstable nucleus which has excessive ________. (2026)
e: Radionuclides have an unstable nucleus containing excessive energy.

q: The combustion of fossil fuel generates ________ compounds whereas biodiesel does not. (2026)
e: Fossil fuel combustion produces sulphur compounds, unlike biodiesel.

q: Solvent like ________, which is used in dry cleaning of clothes, pollute the groundwater and are carcinogenic. (2026)
e: Tetrachloroethylene (Cl2C=CCl2) is a dry cleaning solvent that pollutes groundwater and acts as a carcinogen.
